images.filename: San Francisco Trip - Aug 2013 - USS Potomac.jpg
images.caption: While watching the traffic in San Francisco Bay, my eye was drawn to this striking vessel.   My first thought was, "Gosh.  That looks like an old Coast Guard Cutter.  Maybe something from the 1930s or 1940s."  Scary.  It actually IS an old Coast Guard Cutter.  It is the former USCGC Electra.  The Electra was built for the Coast Guard in 1934 in Manitowoc, WI.  It was converted in 1936 to the USS Potomac, a presidential yacht operated by the US Navy for Franklin D. Roosevelt.  It served as his yacht until his death in 1945.  It is now a museum/tour boat.  I guess next time in the area, I'll have to go and check it out!
images.alt: While watching the traffic in San Francisco Bay, my eye was drawn to this striking vessel.   My first thought was, "Gosh.  That looks like an old Coast Guard Cutter. images.caption:
The “Floating White House” was originally commissioned the USCG Cutter Electra in 1934.  In 1936 it was renamed the USS Potomac and served as Franklin Delano Roosevelt’s Presidential Yacht until his death in 1945.
More than a quarter of a million people have visited and sailed aboard the former President’s beloved "Floating White House," the USS Potomac, since it opened to the public in the summer of 1995. $5 million was spent over a 12-year period to restore the 50 m (165 ft) long vessel as a memorial to the president who authored the New Deal and led the United States during the Great Depression and the World War II years.
